title: JavaScript Debugging Core Check
description: Check your understanding of console methods, DevTools, breakpoints, stack traces, async debugging, network debugging, DOM events, and performance basics.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Why is it useful to label console output?

options.text: Labels make it clear which value or code path produced the output
Labels are required for `console.log()` to work

questions.explanation: Clear labels make console output easier to identify, especially when several values are logged.

questions.prompt: Which console method is best for displaying an array of similar objects in rows and columns?
questions.explanation: `console.table()` displays tabular data, such as arrays of objects, in a readable table.

questions.prompt: Which DevTools panel is most useful for inspecting request URLs, status codes, headers, payloads, and responses?
questions.explanation: The Network panel shows requests and responses made by the page.

options.text: Pauses JavaScript execution so you can inspect current state
Converts synchronous code into async code

questions.explanation: Breakpoints pause execution at a selected line, allowing you to inspect variables, scope, `this`, and the call stack.

questions.prompt: When should you use Step into instead of Step over?

options.text: When the bug may be inside the function being called
When you want to skip all remaining code
When you want to remove a breakpoint

questions.explanation: Step into enters the called function so you can debug inside it.

options.text: Code tried to use a variable name that is not available in the current scope

questions.explanation: A `ReferenceError` often means a variable was misspelled or used outside the scope where it exists.

questions.prompt: What should you inspect when you see `Cannot read properties of undefined`?

options.text: The value immediately before the property access

questions.explanation: This error means code expected an object but received `undefined`; inspect where that value came from.

questions.prompt: What is a common cause of seeing `Promise { <pending> }` where an object was expected?

options.text: A Promise-producing operation was not awaited
The object has too many properties
The page used too much CSS

questions.explanation: A pending Promise often means an async operation still needs `await` or a `.then()` handler.

questions.prompt: Does `fetch()` reject automatically for HTTP statuses like `404` or `500`?
questions.explanation: `fetch()` usually rejects for network-level failures, not normal HTTP error statuses.

questions.prompt: In an event handler, what is `event.currentTarget`?

options.text: The element whose listener is currently running

questions.explanation: `event.currentTarget` is the element that owns the listener currently handling the event.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of source maps?

options.text: They map bundled or minified code back to original source files

questions.explanation: Source maps help DevTools and stack traces point back to original files after code has been bundled or transformed.

questions.prompt: What is the main goal of a repeatable debugging workflow?

options.text: Replace guesses with evidence and narrow down the root cause
Change as many files as possible quickly
Hide every error with fallback values

questions.explanation: A good workflow helps you reproduce the bug, gather facts, test hypotheses, and fix the cause.
